subject: science

entries: Across period 3, atoms shrink: nuclear charge rises from sodium to argon at nearly constant shielding, so the outer electrons are pulled closer and the atoms get smaller.
slots.label: Across period 3
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Melting point tells the structure story: metallic structures for sodium to aluminium, a giant covalent lattice peaking at silicon, then simple molecular elements with weak intermolecular forces.
slots.label: Melting point
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: First ionisation energy: the rise, and two dips: the general rise follows rising nuclear charge and falling radius; the dips are magnesium to aluminium (3p electron removed) and phosphorus to sulphur (paired-electron repulsion).
slots.label: First ionisation energy
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Down group 2: reactivity climbs: atoms grow larger with more shielding down the group, the outer electrons are lost more easily, and reactivity with water climbs from magnesium to barium.
slots.label: Down group 2
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Down group 17: oxidising power falls: atoms grow larger down the group, an incoming electron is held less strongly, and oxidising power falls from chlorine to iodine.
slots.label: Down group 17
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Colour comes from partially filled d-orbitals: ligands split the d-orbitals into two energy levels, and electrons absorbing visible light as they jump between them give transition-metal ions their colour.
slots.label: Colour
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Ligands crowd the metal; catalysts flip oxidation states: ligands donate lone pairs to form complex ions, and variable oxidation states let transition metals catalyse reactions by flipping between states.
slots.label: Ligands and catalysts
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: A common mistake: zinc is a transition metal: zinc forms only Zn2+, whose 3d subshell is completely filled, so by the ion-based definition zinc is a d-block element but not a transition metal.
slots.label: A common mistake
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Half the distance between the nuclei of two bonded atoms of the element: across period 3 it falls as nuclear charge rises at constant shielding.
slots.label: Atomic radius
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The energy needed to remove one mole of electrons from one mole of gaseous atoms to form gaseous 1+ ions: it rises across period 3, with dips at aluminium and sulphur.
slots.label: First ionisation energy
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The power of an atom to attract the electrons in a covalent bond: it rises across a period as radius falls and nuclear charge grows.
slots.label: Electronegativity
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A species that gains electrons and is itself reduced: the halogens are oxidising agents, strongest at the top of group 17 and weakening down the group.
slots.label: Oxidising agent
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A d-block element that forms at least one stable ion with a partially filled d subshell: the partial filling gives colour, variable oxidation states, complexes and catalysis.
slots.label: Transition metal
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A molecule or ion that donates a lone pair of electrons to a central metal ion, forming a coordinate bond in a complex ion.
slots.label: Ligand
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

title: JC H2 chemistry — inorganic: periodicity, groups and transition metals
